What is a reasonable estimate of the weight of an adult human?
A
7  100
N
B
7  102
N
C
7  104
N
D
7  106
N

hints: Start from a typical adult mass in $\text{kg}$ - think of about $70 \text{ kg}$ rather than $7 \text{ kg}$ or $7000 \text{ kg}$.
Connect mass to weight in $\text{N}$ using $W = mg$ with $g \approx 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ on Earth.
Multiply your $70 \text{ kg}$ estimate by $10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ and check which power of ten, $10^0$, $10^2$, $10^4$ or $10^6$, it is closest to.
walkthrough: Estimate the mass of an adult human as about $m \approx 70 \text{ kg}$.
State the rule for weight: $W = mg$, where $g \approx 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $W$ is in $\text{N}$.
Substitute the estimate: $W \approx 70 \text{ kg} \times 10 \text{ m s}^{-2} = 700 \text{ N}$.
Write in powers of ten: $700 \text{ N} = 7 \times 10^2 \text{ N}$, which matches the order of magnitude of the estimate.

A.explanation: $7 \times 10^0 \text{ N} = 7 \text{ N}$ is the weight of a mass of about $0.7 \text{ kg}$, far too small for an adult.

B.explanation: A $70 \text{ kg}$ adult has weight $W = mg \approx 700 \text{ N} = 7 \times 10^2 \text{ N}$.

C.explanation: $7 \times 10^4 \text{ N}$ would need a mass of about $7000 \text{ kg}$, similar to a large truck, not a human.

D.explanation: $7 \times 10^6 \text{ N}$ would need a mass of about $700000 \text{ kg}$, millions of times too large.
